findings.title: Unenforced quoting-enclave identity
findings.description: A verifier fetched quoting-enclave identity collateral but never enforced it, allowing unauthorized quoting-enclave evidence to pass as trusted.

findings.title: Optional consensus field caused a next-height enclave dead end
findings.description: An optional consensus field controlled the only enclave write required at the next height, letting one Byzantine proposer commit a block the network could not advance past.

findings.title: Malformed transaction reached an enclave before generic decoding
findings.description: A pre-decode SGX path parsed proposer-controlled transaction bytes with an unrecoverable failure, allowing one malformed byte to halt block finalization.

findings.title: Cross-layer parser failure in a TEE-assisted consensus path
findings.description: Insufficient validation at a trusted-execution boundary allowed malformed consensus input to trigger a network-wide availability failure.

findings.title: Authorization smuggling across a TEE migration boundary
findings.description: An authorization gap across a trusted-execution workflow could let an untrusted party cross a sensitive trust boundary and access protected network material.

findings.title: Non-atomic cross-domain state transition
findings.description: A failed cross-system operation could leave inconsistent state behind, allowing value-affecting effects to be applied more than once.

findings.title: Missing TCB-status enforcement
findings.description: A verifier exposed platform security status without enforcing rejection, allowing revoked or outdated TCB states to be treated permissively.

findings.title: GPU attestation without complete cryptographic verification
findings.description: GPU evidence was presented as verified without complete certificate-chain validation or cryptographic binding to the trusted CPU environment.

findings.title: Verifier-side SSRF through untrusted collateral routing
findings.description: An untrusted collateral endpoint let callers redirect verifier-side requests toward internal services and metadata endpoints.

findings.title: Misleading event-log verification semantics
findings.description: Cryptographic digest replay was labeled as event-log verification even though attacker-controlled human-readable semantics were not independently validated.

findings.title: Validator-memory exhaustion through an incomplete iterator bound
findings.description: A resource limit constrained the wrong dimension, allowing bounded-looking input to exhaust validator memory and disrupt network progress.

findings.title: Compact-input memory amplification during decoding
findings.description: A small structured input could expand into disproportionate memory use during validation, causing validators to fail on the same block.

findings.title: Aggregate-certificate validation disagreed with downstream vote processing
findings.description: Two stages of consensus validation interpreted the same participation evidence differently, allowing invalid input to influence vote processing.

findings.title: TLS verification disabled for attestation collateral
findings.description: Collateral retrieval could operate without TLS certificate verification, exposing trust inputs to network interception or substitution.

findings.title: Unauthenticated certificate-revocation data
findings.description: A verifier parsed certificate-revocation lists without authenticating their issuer or signature, letting attacker-controlled collateral determine revocation outcomes.

findings.title: Inverted platform-security comparator
findings.description: An inverted TCB comparison could accept stale platform firmware while rejecting patched systems, and required coordinated fixes in both Go and Rust.

findings.title: Host-side VM work escaped protocol gas accounting
findings.description: Security-sensitive execution work occurred outside protocol resource accounting, allowing ordinary inputs to consume disproportionate validator CPU.

findings.title: Unbounded lifecycle cleanup became a consensus-time failure
findings.description: Attacker-influenced state could accumulate until a routine lifecycle transition required unbounded work, threatening validator availability.

findings.title: Stale cross-index references triggered deterministic node panics
findings.description: Inconsistent bookkeeping between related block-processing structures allowed adversarial network input to trigger deterministic node failures.

findings.title: Missing attestation-freshness enforcement
findings.description: A Rust verifier omitted the freshness bound enforced by its Go counterpart, allowing stale attestations beyond the configured age window.

findings.title: Unbounded event data retained in consensus memory
findings.description: A valid execution path allowed attacker-controlled output data to exceed practical memory bounds and repeatedly disrupt validators.

findings.title: Authenticated request could steer expensive work to an unrelated context
findings.description: An authenticated request was insufficiently bound to the work it authorized, enabling attacker-directed resource consumption.
